The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals met to hear several residential petitions, granting variances for multi-family expansion projects at 15 Hadley Place and 54 South Street as well as a special permit to rebuild a fire-damaged four-family structure at 80 Canal Street.
k: Continued Matters: 436 Riverside Ave and 590 Boston Ave
Special Permit Application for 80 Canal Street

docs.o: The commission reviewed the progress of citywide bike lane striping, approved the purchase of bike light kits, and coordinated volunteers for upcoming community events.
k: Winthrop Street Feedback and Intersection Safety

docs.o: The Community Preservation Committee introduced three new members and approved funding for four projects, including major allocations for affordable housing and school playground renovations.
Medford Bytes interviewed School Committee candidate Aaron Olapade regarding his candidate platform, background in community service, approach to school safety, and vision for curriculum reform.
k: Candidate Background and Motivation to Run

docs.o: The Community Development Board approved a site plan for an H Mart grocery store, recommended proposed zoning ordinance amendments to the City Council, and received an update on MBTA Communities overlay planning.
k: Site Plan Review for 285-295 Middlesex Avenue
Special Permit Continuance for 3850 Mystic Valley Parkway

docs.o: The Medford Conservation Commission welcomed a new member and reviewed several wetland permitting applications and compliance requests. The commission approved a driveway replacement at 69 South Street, a 40B residential development at 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway, two certificates of compliance, and an amended order of conditions for a bicycle path extension.
k: Notice of Intent - 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway
Certificates of Compliance - 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway and Commercial Street Extension
Amended Notice of Intent - Bicycle Path Extension

docs.t: City Council Committee of the Whole 08-15-23
docs.b: CC City Council Meeting of the Whole
docs.o: The Committee of the Whole met to review proposed updates to Medford's solid waste ordinance under Paper 22-605. The committee approved draft amendments and voted to refer the ordinance out of committee for legal and departmental review.

The Medford City Council approved a Planned Development District rezoning on Winchester Street, referred a second PDD proposal on Mystic Avenue to the Community Development Board, and ordained a multi-year wage agreement for DPW union workers. The Council also discussed citywide rodent control measures and approved local business license petitions.
k: Committee Report on Solid Waste Collection Contract
Continued Public Hearing on Zoning Ordinance Amendments
Public Hearing on Winchester Street Planned Development District
Planned Development District Referral for 243 Mystic Avenue
Common Victualler's License for Mystic Market
Resolution on Citywide Rodent Infestation Control
DPW Collective Bargaining Wage Adjustment Ordinance
Placing Citizens Bank ADA Ramp Petition on File

docs.o: The Medford Historical Commission reviewed site plans for 421 High Street, discussed historic documentation for the proposed Walkling Court redevelopment, and approved funding for a historic property survey on Court Street.
k: Walkling Court MHC Form A Review
Properties Under Demolition Delay and 67-69 Court Street
CPA Grant Applications and Inventory Survey Updates

docs.o: The Medford School Committee approved the appointment of Gerald McHugh as interim director of finance before voting to enter executive session to discuss collective bargaining, non-unit administrative contracts, and security matters.
k: Appointment of Interim Director of Finance

docs.o: The commission reviewed the resubmission timeline and hearing schedule for the South Street Historic District. Members also agreed to request a city staff executive secretary to handle administrative tasks and minutes.
k: South Street Historic District Application and Hearing Scheduling

docs.o: The Charter Study Committee subcommittee met to define its scope and assign research tasks regarding city council composition and hybrid ward representation. Members reviewed historical ward-by-ward voter turnout data and delegated individual research topics to prepare draft language for the full committee.

Hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan interviewed City Council candidate Emily Lazzaro regarding her platform and professional background. Lazzaro emphasized her priorities of increasing city revenue, improving school funding, and expanding municipal social services for housing and addiction.
k: Background and Motivation for Council Run

docs.t: Fine Arts Program- Medford High School
docs.o: The Medford High School Fine Arts Department presented an informational orientation video detailing its course offerings, faculty, and student studio experiences. Department coordinator Mrs. Fee and several students highlighted electives including ceramics, design, drawing and painting, sculpture, AP art, and photography.
The committee established a subcommittee to research a hybrid ward-based representation model and adopted a new policy for real-time public participation during meetings.

The Community Development Board recommended two proposed Planned Development District rezonings at 243 Mystic Avenue and 100 Winchester Street to the City Council. The board also continued public hearings on a site plan review for H Mart and proposed municipal zoning ordinance amendments.
k: 243 Mystic Avenue Planned Development District Rezoning
285–295 Middlesex Avenue (H Mart) Site Plan Review
100 Winchester Street Planned Development District Rezoning
City Council Petition for Zoning Ordinance Amendments
Administrative Business, Approval of Minutes, and Staff Updates

docs.o: The Medford Conservation Commission convened without a quorum and voted to continue its single agenda item to August 16, 2023.
k: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway Notice of Intent

docs.t: City Highlights from Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn 8-2-2023
docs.o: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn introduced multilingual community connectors from the Board of Health, who highlighted city assistance programs, MassHealth renewals, and upcoming English classes for residents.
k: Board of Health Multilingual Community Connectors

docs.o: The Medford Bicycle Advisory Commission met to discuss upcoming community events, design concerns for the proposed Mystic River Pedestrian Bridge, strategies to encourage cycling to Medford High School, and citywide infrastructure updates.
k: Bike lane enforcement and vegetation trimming

docs.t: City Council Committee of the Whole 07-25-23
docs.b: CC City Council Meeting of the Whole
docs.o: The committee reviewed a proposed 10-year solid waste contract that introduces citywide weekly food composting and a planned transition to bi-weekly trash collection in year three. DPW and Planning officials detailed fiscal strategies to offset rising costs, including new fees for bulky items and a preferred hauler program for business districts.
k: Overview of the Solid Waste RFP
Proposed Weekly Food Composting and Bi-weekly Trash
Rodent Control and Waste Container Security
Commercial District Waste and Preferred Hauler Program
Changes to Bulky Item and Yard Waste Collection

docs.o: The City Council authorized the mayor to enter into a 10-year solid waste and composting agreement and approved a new council rule allowing outside consultant fees to be charged to special permit applicants. The council also approved common victualler licenses and debated recent road safety interventions at Winthrop Street and Playstead Road.
k: Winthrop Street and Playstead Road Interventions

docs.t: City Highlights from Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn 7-25-2023
docs.o: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn provided updates on city park renovations, heat wave emergency preparations, and the appointment of the city's next Poet Laureate.

Hosts interviewed City Council candidate Anna Callahan about her professional background in software and political organizing. Callahan outlined a platform focused on community engagement, climate resilience, housing, and progressive financial reform.
The Community Development Board approved a site plan for an academic addition at Tufts University under the Dover Amendment and conducted internal elections for board leadership.
k: Continuances for Verdant Bio, H Mart, and Bank of America
Staff Updates and Site Visit Procedures

docs.o: The School Committee deliberated on and approved a revised Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan Policy, focusing on the definition of bullying, caregiver notification, and language accessibility. The body adopted several amendments to ensure parents receive incident reports and have access to translation services during investigations.
k: Record Keeping and Civil Rights Information

docs.o: The Board approved revisions to solid waste, recycling, and dumpster regulations to align with city ordinances and state environmental standards. The updates include new reporting requirements for waste haulers and pest management mandates for dumpster permits.

The Commission approved a preliminary report for submission to the Massachusetts Historical Commission and planned public outreach for an upcoming hearing. The body coordinated mailings to district residents and abutters ahead of a scheduled public hearing in September.

The board approved a side yard setback variance for a sunroom on Gadsden Street and dimensional variances for a mixed-use redevelopment on High Street. It denied a front yard parking variance on Alexander Street and continued several matters due to pending reviews and lack of quorum.

The council approved a zoning change for 99 Revere Beach Parkway to allow mixed-use development and denied a $500,000 rate subsidy from water and sewer reserves. The meeting also included honors for a lifesaving rescue at a city pool and discussion of heavy truck traffic on residential streets.
k: 99 Revere Beach Parkway Zoning Map Change
Water and Sewer Enterprise Fund Subsidy

docs.o: The Commission approved a 7% rate increase for fiscal year 2024, utilizing a $500,000 budget transfer to mitigate the impact on residents. The meeting also addressed a significant hardship abatement request for a residential pipe burst and the necessity of a 10-year capital plan for infrastructure replacement.
The board reviewed and approved a draft decision for a 350-unit residential development under MGL Chapter 40B, following deliberations on infrastructure waivers and public art conditions.
k: Factual Findings and Fire Safety Conditions
Public Art and Indigenous History Consultation

docs.o: The commission denied significance for 23 Winter Street, released 31 South Street from demolition delay, and voted to fund new historic inventory work in the Winter Hill neighborhood. Members also discussed a major development at 243 Mystic Avenue and proposed ordinance changes to automate significance for pre-1900 buildings.
k: 243 Mystic Avenue Proposed Development District Review
CPA Projects and Cemetery Restoration Updates

docs.t: City Highlights from Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn 7-10-2023
docs.o: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn provided updates on the city's summer recreational offerings, ongoing road maintenance across 150 streets, and the status of several park renovation projects.
City Council candidate Matt Leming discussed his campaign platform, focusing on the housing crisis, city charter reform, and increasing public participation in municipal government.
k: Charter Study Committee and Governance Reform

docs.o: Incoming Roberts Elementary School Principal Michelle Crowell introduced herself to the school community and shared her background and educational priorities.
Principal Jennifer Skane introduces herself to the community and outlines the academic programs, extracurricular activities, and educational philosophy at Andrews Middle School.
Medford High School Principal Marta Cabral introduced herself to the school community, sharing her educational background, values, and vision for student engagement and partnerships with families.

The Medford Charter Study Committee met to review public participation rules, its draft work plan, and a public survey. The committee voted to continue focusing on a mayor-led executive branch rather than a city manager system unless public input directs otherwise.
k: New Member Status and Meeting Minutes
Focus Groups and Input Tracking Sheet

docs.o: The commission welcomed three new members and voted to submit formal feedback on the state's Wellington Circle redesign draft report. The body also moved to re-submit a prioritized bike rack installation list to city departments and received updates on local paving and safety signage.
